findings.summary: Every topic's opening definition falls at the bottom of the previous page, so from page 2 onward each page's title, hero icon and subtitle describe a different service than most of its body.
findings.evidence: Page 2 is titled "AWS IAM" / hero "iam" but its last block is "EC2 provides ==resizable compute capacity==; launch virtual servers (instances) and run applications."; page 3 is titled "IAM Policies" / subtitle "Policies and Permissions" / hero "iam" yet its "1. Key Concepts" cards are "AMI", "Instance", "Instance Types", "On-Demand", "Reserved", "Spot". The same offset repeats: page 4 ("EC2 Compute") ends with the S3 definition, page 5 ("S3 Object Storage") ends with the database intro and "1. RDS", page 8 ("VPC Networking") ends with the advanced-networking intro, page 9 ends with "1. EBS".
findings.fix: Re-paginate so each service starts at the top of the page that carries its title and hero: move the EC2 intro paragraph to the head of page 3 and retitle page 3 "EC2 - Compute", move the S3 intro to the head of page 5, the database intro to the head of page 6/7, the networking intro to the head of page 9, and the storage intro to the head of page 10 — or keep the current titles and move the trailing paragraphs forward to match.

findings.summary: The title "IAM Policies" misdescribes a page whose body is EC2 fundamentals, not IAM policy content.
findings.evidence: Page 3 ("page_title": "IAM Policies") contains headings "1. Key Concepts" (cards: AMI, Instance, Instance Types, On-Demand, Reserved, Spot, Security Group, Key Pair, User Data, Tags), "2. Instance Lifecycle", "3. Pricing Options", "4. Storage Options", "5. Architecture"; the only IAM material is two lead bullets ("Roles give ==temporary credentials==...", "Resources identified by ARN..."). Actual IAM policy sections ("6. Policy Structure", "7. Policy Effect") live on page 2.
findings.fix: Retitle page 3 to "EC2 Essentials" (and update the carousel titles array accordingly), or move the two trailing IAM-role/ARN bullets onto page 2 and start page 3 cleanly at the EC2 key-concepts block.

findings.summary: Page 8 ends with three unlabelled diagrams for Route 53, ELB and CloudFront whose defining sections only appear on page 9, so the learner sees the pictures before any of the three services is named or explained.
findings.evidence: Page 8's final blocks are bare diagrams — {"nodes":["www.example.com","Route 53","192.0.2.10"]}, {"nodes":["Users","Load Balancer","Targets/Instances"]}, {"nodes":["Users Worldwide","Edge Locations","S3/Origin"]} — with no heading between them; page 9 then opens with heading "1. Route 53" ("Scalable DNS; converts domain names to IP"), "2. Elastic Load Balancing", "3. CloudFront".
findings.fix: Move the three diagrams onto page 9 and place each one directly beneath its own heading (Route 53 flow under "1. Route 53", the load balancer flow under "2. Elastic Load Balancing", the edge-location flow under "3. CloudFront").

findings.summary: The Aurora deep-dive page runs before Aurora is introduced, so cluster-volume internals and an Aurora-vs-RDS comparison precede the sentence that first says what Aurora is.
findings.evidence: Page 6 opens with "Aurora Primary" replicas and "Cluster volume auto-grows in ==10 GB== steps, up to 128 TB", "Keeps **6 copies** of data across 3 Availability Zones", plus an "Aurora vs RDS" table; page 7 then begins with heading "2. Aurora" and the beginner bullets "MySQL and PostgreSQL compatible", "High performance, auto-scaling storage", "Up to 15 read replicas, Multi-AZ cluster".
findings.fix: Place the "2. Aurora" introduction bullets before the deep-dive page: move page 6 to sit after page 7's Aurora section, or fold the three intro bullets into the top of page 6 and delete the duplicate "2. Aurora" block on page 7. The deep-dive page also drops back to "1. Storage & Replication" numbering mid-chapter — renumber it to continue the database chapter's sequence.

findings.summary: The sample route table lists two conflicting default routes, which AWS rejects because a route table cannot contain duplicate destination CIDRs.
findings.evidence: "5. Route Table" table rows: ["10.0.0.0/16","local"], ["0.0.0.0/0","Internet Gateway"], ["0.0.0.0/0","NAT Gateway"]
findings.fix: Split into two tables — a public route table (10.0.0.0/16 → local, 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway) and a private route table (10.0.0.0/16 → local, 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway) — and label which subnet each is associated with.

findings.summary: The S3 section of the storage chapter is missing its heading and bullets — the page opens with an S3 bucket diagram that nothing introduces.
findings.evidence: Page 10's first block is {"type":"diagram","kind":"flow","spec":{"nodes":["S3 Bucket","Image","Doc","Video"]}}, immediately followed by heading "Glacier Retrieval Tiers"; page 9 ended at "1. EBS", so no "2. S3" heading or object-storage bullets exist between them.

findings.summary: The title "Inside an S3 Bucket" misdescribes a page that is mostly non-S3 file and hybrid storage services.
findings.evidence: Page 10's blocks after the opening "S3 Bucket -> Image/Doc/Video" flow are "Glacier Retrieval Tiers", "Storage Gateway" (File/Volume/Tape gateways), "EFS - Shared File Storage" ("Managed ==NFS== file storage for Linux"), and "FSx - Managed File Systems".
findings.fix: Retitle page 10 to something covering its actual scope, e.g. "Glacier, Storage Gateway, EFS & FSx" — matching the sibling title already used in part 02, "S3, EFS & FSx Storage".

findings.summary: The series title omits the part number that every other part in this series carries.

findings.summary: YubiKey is given as the example of a hardware TOTP MFA device, but AWS classifies YubiKey under FIDO security keys — the separate bullet on the same list.

findings.summary: The EC2 architecture diagram uses "Elastic IP" a page before Elastic IP is defined.
findings.evidence: Page 3, "5. Architecture": {"text":"EC2 Instance","sub":"Elastic IP","ink":"orange"}; the definition appears only on page 4 — "2. Elastic IP" / "Static public IPv4, survives restarts".

findings.summary: ARN is used in a policy example on page 2 and then referenced as a bare acronym on page 3 without ever being expanded.
findings.evidence: Page 2's policy code block contains "\"Resource\": [\"arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket\"]" with the note "Effect, Action, Resource are required"; page 3 then says "Resources identified by ARN, e.g. `arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/*`" — the expansion "Amazon Resource Name" appears nowhere.
findings.fix: Expand on first use: annotate the page 2 policy example's Resource line with "ARN (Amazon Resource Name)" and keep page 3's bullet as the follow-up detail.

findings.summary: The ElastiCache engine list omits Valkey, which is now a first-class ElastiCache engine (and AWS's default recommendation over Redis OSS).
findings.evidence: "Supports Redis and Memcached"
findings.fix: Change to "Supports Valkey, Redis OSS and Memcached".

findings.summary: The DynamoDB and "When to Use" sections rely on acronyms (RCU/WCU, GSI, LSI, ACID) that are never expanded or explained anywhere in the handbook.
findings.evidence: Page 7: "Auto scales, uses RCU/WCU"; "Indexes: GSI and LSI"; "ACID transactions -> RDS/Aurora".
findings.fix: Expand each on first use — "read/write capacity units (RCU/WCU)", "Global Secondary Index (GSI) and Local Secondary Index (LSI)", and a one-line gloss for ACID (atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability) next to the RDS/Aurora recommendation.

findings.summary: Elastic Load Balancing is re-introduced at beginner level on page 9 after page 4 already gave the full ALB/NLB/CLB comparison, and the newly added GWLB is left unexpanded.
findings.evidence: Page 4 has "9. LB Comparison" with rows "Layer | 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) | 4 (TCP/UDP) | 4 and 7"; page 9's "2. Elastic Load Balancing" then restates "Distributes incoming traffic across targets", "Improves availability, fault tolerance, scalability", "Types: ALB, NLB, GWLB, CLB".
findings.fix: On page 9, cut the restated basics, keep only what is new — "GWLB (Gateway Load Balancer): runs third-party virtual appliances inline" — and point back to the page 4 comparison table.
